note: if/else in three languages. This case exists because the rosetta gate caught rust modelling `else` inline while python and typescript gave it a node — a shared-names violation that made `alternative:` mean different things per language and left `(_clause)` a member short. `(_clause)` is asserted here, unlike hello-roles, precisely because these programs use only the clause all three share.
field_query_note: the obvious guard, `(_branch alternative: (else_clause))`, is NOT asserted: tree-sitter 0.26 rejects it as an impossible pattern because a field named through a supertype must exist on EVERY subtype, and `_branch` also covers match/switch, which have no `alternative:`. `(_declaration body: (_body))` is asserted instead — the same shape where every subtype does agree — so the working and failing cases are both visible here. Note the CLI we generate with (0.25.10) still accepts the rejected form, so this is also a toolchain skew: see the ledger.
